title: ED Triage Nursing Note
author: J. Whitaker, RN
summary: Arrived 0030 with his roommate: vomiting all day Sunday after a weekend of drinking; insulin pump set found pulled half out. Deep fast breathing, fruity breath. POC glucose 556. ESI 2.
body:
**Arrival 0030** by private car with his roommate (Theo Grant), who found him "breathing weird and not making sense" when he got home from work at about 2345.

**Story (Jordan and roommate)**
- Type 1 diabetes since age 11, on a tubed insulin pump with a CGM.
- Saturday night: friend's birthday, about 10-12 drinks (beer and shots) from about 2100 to 0200, ate little. Fell asleep on a friend's couch in his clothes; his phone died, so he did not hear CGM alarms.
- Sunday: woke about 1000, vomiting from about 1100 ("8-10 times"), belly ache, thought it was a hangover. CGM high all day; gave two correction boluses through the pump (about 1300 and 1700). Did not check ketones (no strips at home). No backup insulin pen that works and no long-acting insulin at home.
- No fever, cough or diarrhea. Denies drugs. Allergy: penicillin (hives as a child).

**Triage 0035**
T 99.0 F, HR 122, BP 104/62, RR 28 deep and regular (Kussmaul), SpO2 98% room air, pain 5/10 upper belly, headache 3/10. Weight 72.0 kg (bed scale). Sleepy but answers; GCS 15. Fruity (acetone) breath, no smell of alcohol. Dry mouth.

**Insulin pump**: infusion set on the left lower abdomen half pulled off; adhesive lifted and wet; insulin smell on the dressing; tubing twisted around his belt loop.

**POC glucose 0040: 556.**

ESI 2. To room 12; Dr. Castillo at the bedside 0040. DKA order set.

title: ED Nursing Note - DKA Treatment and Response
author: J. Whitaker, RN
summary: Moderate DKA treated per the adult protocol: 1 L saline, then lactated Ringer's; insulin 7.2 units/h fixed from 0215 (no bolus); KCl 20 mEq/L from 0400 once K 4.6. Pump suspended and removed 0110. Glucose falling about 50 per hour.
body:
**Lines**
- 0045: 18 g IV left forearm (labs drawn first).
- 0050: 20 g IV right antecubital (saline lock: IV push and potassium riders).

**Insulin pump**
- 0110: pump SUSPENDED and disconnected; old set removed (cannula bent, adhesive wet). Pump, tubing and old set in a labeled bag with his belongings. Site: small red dot, no infection. His CGM sensor (back of right arm) left on; his phone is charging.

**Treatment**
- 0055-0155 normal saline 1,000 mL.
- 0100 ondansetron 4 mg IV. 0105 thiamine 100 mg IV (before any dextrose).
- 0115 ECG: sinus tach 118, tall T waves (K 5.4). Void 450 mL (urine sample and drug screen).
- 0130 vomited 200 mL clear.
- 0200 lactated Ringer's 500 mL/h (no potassium yet: K 5.4).
- **0215 regular insulin infusion 7.2 units/h (0.1 unit/kg/h), no bolus**, own pump, tubing primed. Independent double check with S. Patel, RN.
- 0330 void 500 mL.
- 0400 lactated Ringer's with KCl 20 mEq/L at 250 mL/h (K 4.6 at 0300, voiding).
- 0545 void 400 mL.
- 0630 BMP, Mg, phos, VBG, BHB, lactate drawn (pending).

**Response**
- POC glucose: 556 (0040), 518 (0200), 476 (0300), 422 (0400), 368 (0500), 316 (0600): falling 52-54 per hour on insulin.
- Vitals 0615: HR 106, BP 112/68, RR 24 (less deep), SpO2 98%, T 98.8 F. GCS 15, more awake. CIWA-Ar 2 at 0130 (nausea, mild headache), no tremor.
- I&O since 0030: IV in 2,750 mL + IV meds 86 mL; urine 1,350 mL; emesis 200 mL.

**Patient**
Embarrassed ("I know better"). Asking for his pump back and for food and a soda: told the pump stays off while the IV insulin runs, and only ice chips and sips of water for now. Roommate went home at 0300; mother (Karen Ellis) updated by phone with his permission.

title: ED to IMCU Handoff (SBAR)
author: J. Whitaker, RN
summary: SBAR to the IMCU: moderate DKA from pump failure + weekend drinking; insulin 7.2 units/h, LR + KCl 20 at 250 mL/h; glucose 316 at 0600; 0630 labs pending; D10 when glucose under 250.
body:
**S:** Jordan Ellis, 24, type 1 diabetes on an insulin pump, **moderate DKA** after his infusion set pulled out overnight Saturday, plus a weekend of heavy drinking. Full Code. **Allergy: penicillin (hives).** Weight 72.0 kg.

**B:** pH 7.22, bicarbonate 10, anion gap 26, BHB 6.2, glucose 572, K 5.4, creatinine 1.4 (0045). Ethanol none detected. Lipase normal. HbA1c pending. Pump suspended and in his belongings bag; his own CGM is on (trends only).

**A:**
- Insulin regular **7.2 units/h** since 0215 (fixed rate, no bolus).
- **LR + KCl 20 mEq/L at 250 mL/h** (left forearm). When glucose is under 250: start the **D10 line at 100 mL/h** and turn the LR down to 100 mL/h.
- Glucose 316 at 0600, falling about 50 per hour: expect under 250 around 0730-0800.
- K 4.6 at 0300. **0630 labs drawn, results about 0715.**
- Vitals 0615: HR 106, BP 112/68, RR 24, SpO2 98%, T 98.8.
- IV 2,750 mL + meds 86 in; urine 1,350, emesis 200 out.
- CIWA-Ar 2. Last drink Sunday about 0200.

**R:** Hourly glucose; watch potassium (**peripheral IVs only: riders max 10 mEq/h**); his pump stays off; he is hungry and will push for food and soda. Roommate Theo brings his charger and pump supplies later today.
